title: Databricks profile URI auth must pass the profile to the SDK Config, not only the host
answers: databricks://<profile> tracing uses the wrong Databricks CLI profile
Codex tracing authenticates with the wrong profile when several profiles share one workspace host
MLflow Databricks auth ignores my CLI profile and picks another profile for the same host
body:
Symptom: With tracking URI `databricks://<profile>`, MLflow authenticates with a different CLI profile whenever several profiles point at the same workspace host.
Root cause: libs/typescript/core/src/auth/index.ts:createDatabricksAuth built `new Config({...})` with `host: options.host`, so the SDK ran `databricks auth token --host` instead of `--profile`.
Fix pattern: Pass the resolved host variable to Config, and keep `profile` set. The SDK then calls `databricks auth token --profile <profile>`. This needs @databricks/sdk-experimental 0.18.0, since 0.15.0 authenticated by host.
Constraints: Keep `profile` in the Config alongside `host`. Covered by the regression test in libs/typescript/core/tests/core/auth.test.ts ("passes the tracking URI profile to Databricks CLI authentication"), which asserts the CLI args include `--profile` and not `--host`.
applies: Any change to Databricks credential resolution in @mlflow/core auth, including Codex and other integrations that build on it.
says: Connecting with a specific profile authenticates against the wrong credentials for this workspace.
Tracking signs in using another profile when multiple accounts share one workspace host.
Ensure the configured profile is used instead of falling back to host authentication.
Workspace connection uses credentials from an unintended account sharing the same server URL.
Selecting a connection profile fails to authenticate with the chosen account credentials.
search: Databricks tracking URI authentication in @mlflow/core must supply profile alongside host to the SDK Config object. In libs/typescript/core/src/auth/index.ts:createDatabricksAuth, passing only host causes the SDK to execute databricks auth token --host, resolving incorrect credentials when multiple CLI profiles share a workspace host. Supplying profile requires @databricks/sdk-experimental 0.18.0 so the SDK invokes databricks auth token --profile <profile>. This guidance applies to Databricks credential resolution in @mlflow/core auth and integrations like Codex, verified by libs/typescript/core/tests/core/auth.test.ts.
